让你的Agent变得更聪明其实很简单，只需要装上Memmy，你电脑上所有文件、操作记录、Agent 聊天记录就能长期复利！

Memmy是一个开源的个人记忆中枢+ AI Agent，我已经用了好久了，记忆这块一骑绝尘，可以说AI时代必装工具之一：

⓵记忆跟着人走，打通所有Agent，换一个Agent所有记忆无缝衔接
一般人换一个Agent都要复制一份背景和记忆，但是Memmy打通了Codex、Claude Code、Cursor和DSH这些主流Agent，每一个Agent的记忆都会自动总结沉淀到Memmy，统一管理，就不会再出现换个Agent就失忆的情况～

⓶Computer History保存电脑操作记录
有点类似Codex的Computer History，但统一集成在Memmy里面，更加方便！就比如我现在写这篇推文的所有操作，全部被记录存档在Memmy里面了。

⓷支持接入自定义模型，还能打通微信聊天记录
Memmy 如果是收集隐私数据，我确实不敢用…但是它支持接入自己的 api，我就放心多了，直接接入一手 Deepseek 的 api，爽用！

而且还支持打通微信，可以读取微信聊天记录，原理是拿密钥解析本地数据库，相对安全，和我的 skill 是一个原理。

上述所有的聊天记录和电脑操作历史，还会被沉淀为用户偏好、经验和可复用技能，在 App 内部一目了然，非常方便管理。

最棒的还是 Memmy 还能主动识别电脑上正在执行哪些任务！对于我这种 ADHD 非常友好，多线并行工作，也不会忘掉之前在干啥。

WTF！每天 100 万自然流播放、20 万美元 ARR🤯 X 每天的干货真的学不完，这篇文章讲解了一套 TikTok 和 Instagram 矩阵自动化运营放大打法。

不仅把 Instagram 的 Trial Reels 机制玩明白了，整套工作流也非常清晰高效：
1、素材准备：集中 2-3 天录制一个月的视频素材，多机位和 B-roll 都拍齐。
2、Claude Code 批量剪辑：用 Fable 5.2 给每条视频换不同 hook 和时长，自动切成 6 个测试版本（外加 1 个更短的 TikTok 版）。
3、Edits 配乐：Instagram 官方配套剪辑 App，多次发布相似视频更少被风控。
4、多平台自动分发：Claude 连接 Postiz，把一整月 200+ 视频自动排进 Trial Reels 和 TikTok（还能定时自动发首评）。
5、挑出优胜视频：每隔两天从 Trial Reels 找出播放最高的版本，把 hook 记下来，并把这条视频重新上传到主账号 Reels。

article.plain_text:
Our app crossed $200k ARR
Every dollar came from short form video. Instagram trial reels and TikTok.
And we don't sit on our phones posting all day.
We spend a few days filming and setting up. Then a full month of content goes out on its own.
Every version of every video. Every trial reel. Every TikTok. On time, every day, while we work on the app.
This article is the full system. How we film, how one video turns into 6, how every version gets finished, and how a whole month of posts goes out without us touching it.
If you haven't read our full guide, it's pinned. That one covers the strategy:  the app, the method, the CTA. This one is the machine that runs it.
Proof:
 
 
Before we start
This article shows you what we do.
It won't cover every scenario. Your content might be slideshows, static images, UGC, whatever. Take our flow and apply it to yours.
And we're not experts.
We figured all of this out ourselves. Anyone can do it.
All you need to do is think about the flow:
what do you want automated
what has to happen at each step
what does the end result look like
Then talk to your LLM about it. Ask it how to build it, what prompts you need, how to test it.
Once it's running you'll notice things. "This would be way better if X happened here." So go back, add it, adjust.
Your system will keep getting better the more you use it.
Use this article for inspiration and some guidance, then build your own version.
Let's get into it.
What's inside
Step 1: The system in one picture
Step 2: Film a month in a few days
Step 3: The system cuts every video into 6
Step 4: Finish every version in Edits
Step 5: Distribution is the real bottleneck
Step 6: Schedule the whole month in one go
Step 7: Pick the winner every second day
The month at a glance
The complete system
Step 1: The system in one picture
Here's what goes out, every single day:
Every version of that day's video as an Instagram trial reel (about 6)
1 TikTok, with its own cut
And every second day:
The trial reel with the most views goes up on our main Instagram as a brand new upload
Do the math on a month.
About 180 trial reels. 30 TikToks. 15 main Reels.
200+ posts a month.
Trial reels are the testing lab. They go to people who don't follow you, so your followers are out of the equation and every video wins or loses on its own. Main Reels only get the proven stuff.
Doing all of this every day without a system is a full time job. Film, edit, export 6 versions, add sounds, upload one by one, write captions, check views, re-upload the winner.
Miss two days and the whole thing stalls.
So we built a system around it. We do the creative work. The system does the rest.
Here's the pipeline:
We film in bulk
Claude Code cuts every video into 6 versions
Sound goes on in Edits
Claude schedules the whole month in one go
Everything posts  automatically
We pick a winner every second day
 
Step 2: Film a month in a few days
Filming every day is the first thing that breaks. Sick day, travel day, lazy day, and there's no video.
So we film in bulk.
We block 2 or 3 days and film everything for the month. About 30 videos.
How we do it:
Write a shot list first. Look at what's working for competitors, what's working in other niches, and what's already winning on your own trial reels. Turn each one into a format on the list.
Film each format a few ways. Different angles, different openings, different energy. More raw material per format means more versions later.
Film extra B-roll. Hands, screens, reactions, walking shots, close ups. B-roll is what lets one video become six.
Name your files properly. Something like format-name_take-1.mov. Boring, but it's what lets the system sort your footage without you babysitting it.
Change outfits between formats. A month of content shot in 3 days shouldn't look like it was shot in 3 days.
Then everything goes into one folder per format. That folder is the input for the whole system.
 
Step 3: The system cuts every video into 6
This is where our speed comes from.
We use Claude for editing. Like I said in the pinned guide, we edited 6 videos in the time it used to take us to edit half of one.
Now it runs as a system.
Every video becomes about 6 versions. Each one changes:
The hook (first 1 to 3 seconds)
The length
Which clips get used
The order of the clips
The on-screen text
Every version is a test. After a week you know which hooks hit, which lengths hold people, and which openings flop.
The setup: Claude Code + ffmpeg
Claude Code runs on your computer, so it can open your footage folders and run ffmpeg, the free tool that trims, joins and adds text to video from the command line.
You don't need to know ffmpeg. Claude writes and runs the commands.
Setup:
Install ffmpeg (free) and Claude Code
One folder per format with the raw clips inside
One recipe file Claude follows every time
Ours looks something like this:
For each folder in /footage, make 6 vertical 9:16 versions.
Version 1: 7 seconds, fast cuts, hook text from hooks.txt line 1.
Version 2: 12 seconds, open on the reaction clip, a different hook.
Version 3: 15 seconds, original clip order, no text for the first second.
Versions 4 to 6: shuffle the clip order and test 3 new hooks from hooks.txt.
Also make one shorter, faster TikTok cut per format.
Save to /exports/[format]/ and name each file with the hook and length.
30 videos go in. About 180 Instagram versions and 30 TikTok cuts come out.
We run it at night and wake up to a full month of versions.
Two things that make it better every week:
hooks.txt. Every time a hook wins on trial reels, it goes in this file. Claude pulls from it next time. The hook bank gets stronger every single week.
Separate platform cuts. TikTok wants shorter, more brain rot, less effort. Instagram wants longer, higher quality, slower. It's in the recipe, so we never export one version for both.
Some videos are too messy for Claude to cut well. We do those ourselves. Still saves hours.
Why not a clipping tool? Most of them are built to pull short clips out of long podcasts and YouTube videos. Our videos are already short. We need the same video re-cut 6 different ways, and that's exactly what Claude Code + ffmpeg does.
 
Step 4: Finish every version in Edits
Claude gets you the cuts. Sound is the finishing step.
Every version goes through Instagram's Edits app before it's scheduled.
Why Edits:
It's free and it's Instagram's own editor
It exports clean, no watermark
In our experience, we get flagged less when posting similar videos multiple times, and Instagram treats videos finished in Edits well
Edits just landed on Mac too, so this is a desk job now. Footage folder on one side, Edits on the other.
The flow:
Import the version
Add the sound
Add auto captions if the version needs them
Export into one folder called /ready
Sound is one of your biggest testing levers, so we pick it ourselves. A tool picking sounds blind will cost you views.
One rule on sound: use the royalty-free tracks in the Edits library or your own audio. Licensed songs can get dropped from exports and muted later, and you'll find out after the post is live.
For the TikTok cut, bake the sound into the file. A scheduled TikTok goes up with the audio that's already in the video.
This is the only part of the month that takes real sitting time. One focused day covers the whole batch.
 
Step 5: Distribution is the real bottleneck
Here's what nobody tells you.
Once you can film in bulk and cut 6 versions of everything, making content stops being the problem.
Posting it becomes the problem.
200+ uploads a month. Each one needs the right cut, the right platform, the right caption, the right time, and the right setting (trial reel or main Reel).
Doing that from your phone every day is where consistency dies. It's how we lost $20k/month the first time. No structure.
So posting is the part we handed off completely. That's what Postiz does for us.
Postiz is a scheduling tool that posts to Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, X and a bunch more from one calendar. You schedule it, it publishes at that time. No phone, no reminders.
What we use it for:
One calendar for the month. Every trial reel, every TikTok, every main Reel on one screen. Gaps jump out instantly.
Trial reels, automatically. When you schedule an Instagram Reel there's a Trial Reel toggle (share only to non-followers first). You choose how it graduates: manually, or automatically based on performance. We leave it on manual because we re-upload our winners fresh.
TikTok direct post. It publishes straight to the profile at the time you set. Nothing sitting in your inbox waiting for you to finish it.
Different cuts per platform. Each channel gets its own video and caption, so the TikTok cut goes to TikTok and the Instagram cut goes to Instagram.
Time slots. Set the times each account normally posts, and the calendar plans around them.
A first comment on Instagram. Schedule a comment on your own post, anywhere from 1 minute to 2 hours after it goes live. Good for a short CTA line on every post without remembering to do it.
Analytics per post. Views, likes, comments and shares for each post and each account, in one place.
 
Step 6: Schedule the whole month in one go
Postiz connects to Claude. You can add Postiz from Claude's connectors, and Claude Code picks it up too. Or one command in the terminal:
claude mcp add --transport http postiz https://mcp.postiz.com/mcp-oauth-dynamic
It opens a browser tab, you sign in to Postiz, and you're in. No API key.
We also installed the Postiz CLI (npm install -g postiz) so Claude can upload the files straight from the /ready folder.
Now Claude can see our accounts, upload the videos, and schedule every post.
So scheduling a month is one message:
Upload everything in /ready to Postiz. For each day, schedule that day's 6 Instagram versions as trial reels with manual graduation, spaced out across our time slots. Schedule the TikTok cut of that day's video as a direct post at 6pm. Use the caption in each file name.
Claude builds the month. Every trial reel goes out with this setting:
{"post_type":"post","is_trial_reel":true,"graduation_strategy":"MANUAL"}
Then we open the calendar in month view, check it, drag anything we don't like, and we're done.
Postiz publishes everything at the set time, even with the laptop closed.
Three tips from setting this up:
Make the first week drafts. Tell Claude to schedule week one as drafts. Check them on the calendar, then switch them on. After that you'll trust it.
Watch your timezone. Postiz uses your browser's timezone. If your audience is somewhere else, set your slots for their time.
Keep the files in Postiz. Everything you upload sits in the media library, so the winner re-uploads in Step 7 are one click.
Your posting month goes from hours on your phone every day to one afternoon of setup.
 
Step 7: Pick the winner every second day
The whole system feeds this one decision. It's the only thing we touch during the month.
Every second day:
Check trial reel views in Instagram insights
Find the version with the most views
Schedule that file as a normal Reel on the main account in Postiz (or tell Claude: "schedule this one as a main Reel at 7pm tonight")
Add its hook to hooks.txt
Upload the winner as a brand new video. Don't publish the trial reel itself.
Sometimes the fresh upload gets fewer views. If it already has decent views, it can get a bigger push. Feel it out.
Then write down why it won. The hook? The sound? The length? The first clip? That note decides what gets filmed next month.
And judge every winner by money too. A video with fewer views can still make more if it converts better. Check downloads and revenue on the days your winners go out.
5 minutes, every second day.
 
The month at a glance
Days 1 and 2: Film
Shot list done the night before. Film everything. Dump it into format folders.
Day 3: Cut
Claude Code runs the recipe overnight. About 180 Instagram versions and 30 TikTok cuts.
Day 4: Finish and schedule
Sound and captions in Edits. Everything into /ready. Claude loads the month into Postiz. Check the calendar.
Every day: 10 minutes
Reply to comments. Glance at views.
Every second day: 5 minutes
Pick the winner. Schedule it on the main account.
End of each week: 30 minutes
Review what won. Update hooks.txt. Start next month's shot list.
A few days of work. A full month of posts.
 
The complete system
Here's everything in one place:
Film in bulk. 2 or 3 days covers the month
Claude Code cuts every video into 6. Different hooks, lengths, clip orders, plus a separate TikTok cut
Finish in Edits. Sound and captions, exported to /ready
Claude loads the month into Postiz. Trial reels, TikToks, captions, time slots
Postiz posts everything automatically. Every day, on time, on every account
Winner every second day. Best trial reel goes to the main account as a fresh upload
Weekly review. Update the hook bank, write the next shot list, run it again
Filming, cutting, testing and picking winners is what got us to $40k/month with $0 on ads. The automation is what keeps it running every day.
Once you can make content in bulk, the bottleneck is getting all of it out on time, every day, without falling off. That's the part Postiz runs for us.
Start this week
Write a shot list and bulk film one day
Set up Claude Code and ffmpeg, and make 6 versions of your first video
Start the Postiz trial, connect Instagram and TikTok, and schedule one week as drafts
Every second day, pick the winner and upload it fresh
It won't be perfect the first month. It doesn't need to be.
The system makes posting automatic. It doesn't film the videos for you.
The hardest thing is consistency. If you can't stay consistent, this won't work.
If this helped, follow @nicholascalez. I post our numbers and what we're testing as we scale.
And repost this to someone building an app.
